report_sentences: # Drag in a simulated laboratory: quadratic air drag modulated by an interaction of reflectance and temperature
A smaller additional effect depends on the product (reflectance − 0.5) × (temperature − 20 °C): the drag coefficient is multiplied by about 1 − 0.0095 (R − 0.5)(T − 20).
- Reflectance was set to 0 or 1, and temperature to −20 or 80, in separate sweeps.
For a black object (reflectance 0), flight time rose with temperature from about 3.5 s at −13 °C to about 4.1 s at 80 °C.
- For a white object (reflectance 1), flight time fell with temperature, from about 3.9 s at −18 °C to about 3.4 s at 75 °C.
Their correlations with the model residuals were all below 0.12 in absolute value, and the larger ones are plausibly absorbed by the reflectance and temperature term.
The relevant properties are mass, radius, shape, reflectance × temperature, air density, height, speed and angle.
I have moderate confidence in the exact form and size of the reflectance × temperature interaction.
